residency.test: Tax resident if you stay or work in Singapore for 183 days or more in the calendar year, or under the two-year and three-year administrative concessions.
residency.worldwide_income: No. Singapore taxes income accrued in or derived from Singapore, and foreign income only if received in Singapore in specific circumstances - foreign-sourced income received by individuals is generally exempt.
residency.non_resident: Non-residents pay the higher of 15% flat on employment income or the resident rates, and 24% on other income.
residency.note: Income is assessed for a Year of Assessment based on the preceding calendar year - YA 2026 assesses 2025 income.

headline.rates: 0% to 24%, reaching the top rate above 1,000,000
headline.cpf: 20% employee and 17% employer for citizens and permanent residents; foreigners on work passes do not contribute
headline.no_capital_gains_tax: Singapore has no capital gains tax

income_tax.name: Individual income tax
income_tax.note: resident rates for Year of Assessment 2026 on 2025 income

standard_deduction.name: Earned income relief
standard_deduction.note: 6,000 if aged 55 to 59 and 8,000 from 60; all personal reliefs together are capped at 80,000

employee.name: CPF employee contribution
employee.note: citizens and permanent residents only, up to the Ordinary Wage ceiling of 7,400 a month in 2025 and the 37,740 annual limit. Foreigners on Employment or S Passes contribute nothing

self_employed.name: MediSave contribution
self_employed.note: compulsory for self-employed citizens and PRs with net trade income above 6,000

capital_gains.trading: gains can be recharacterised as trading income and taxed if the frequency, holding period and financing pattern indicate a trade rather than investment
capital_gains.property: no CGT, but Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty and Seller's Stamp Duty apply on purchase and quick resale
capital_gains.dividends: dividends from Singapore resident companies are exempt under the one-tier system

quirks: Foreign-sourced income received by individuals is generally exempt. Combined with no capital gains tax, this is what actually makes Singapore attractive - not the headline rates, which are unremarkable in the middle brackets.
CPF applies only to citizens and permanent residents. A foreigner and a citizen on the same salary have very different take-home pay, and comparing them without saying which is which is misleading.
Personal reliefs are capped at 80,000 in total. Above that, additional CPF top-ups and SRS contributions give no further relief.

The two-year administrative concession means a stay spanning two calendar years totalling at least 183 days can be treated as resident for both years, which matters a lot for arrivals late in the year.
The Supplementary Retirement Scheme allows deductible contributions of 15,300 for citizens and PRs, or 35,700 for foreigners, which is one of the few real deductions available to expatriates.

reporting.who_must_file: Anyone who receives a filing notification, and anyone with annual income above 22,000 or any self-employment income. Employees of companies in the Auto-Inclusion Scheme have salary data pre-filled.

deadlines.what: E-filing deadline for Year of Assessment 2026 (2025 income)
Employers submit employment income under the Auto-Inclusion Scheme
Payment of the assessed tax, or start a GIRO instalment plan
Tax clearance (Form IR21) for foreign employees leaving Singapore

forms.name: Return for tax residents with employment income
Return of employee's remuneration, filed by the employer
Tax clearance notification for departing foreign employees

documents_to_collect: IR8A from the employer, or confirmation that they are on the Auto-Inclusion Scheme
Records of rental income and allowable expenses
Business accounts if self-employed, kept for five years
Donation receipts to Institutions of a Public Character - deductible at 250% of the amount given

penalties.late_filing: up to 1,000 fine, and an estimated assessment which must still be paid
penalties.late_payment: 5% penalty, plus 1% a month up to 12% additional
penalties.understatement: up to 200% of the undercharged tax; up to 400% with intent to evade
penalties.tax_clearance: the employer must withhold monies from a departing foreign employee until clearance is given

warnings: CPF is modelled as applying at the full rate. Set employment income net of CPF, or ignore the CPF line entirely, for foreigners on work passes who do not contribute.
CPF rates fall in bands from age 55 onward and are not age-adjusted here.
Personal reliefs beyond earned income relief (spouse, child, parent, course fees, SRS) are not modelled and are capped at 80,000 in total.
